title: May Ziadeh's birth chart
metaDescription: May Ziadeh's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 22.6° Aquarius. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The Moon stands at 14.0° Taurus, in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best. Of everything the chart can be read for without a birth time, that is the loudest single fact in it.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: The Sun sits at 22.6° Aquarius — the third decan, 20°–30°, which the tradition sub-rules by Venus. Degrees matter more than the sign label here: two people born a fortnight apart share Aquarius and share almost nothing else about where the Sun actually stood.

blocks.title: The fast planets
blocks.text: Mercury holds 12.6° Aquarius, Venus holds 4.5° Pisces, Mars holds 23.5° Virgo — in the old shorthand, a mind at home in argument and pattern; taste tuned to mood and undertow; drive that grinds rather than flares.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: The day's firmest angle joins the Sun and Neptune — a square holding at 0.2°. Nothing in a square flows; everything in it works. The old texts kept squares for the charts they respected. Behind it, Mars trine Neptune at 0.7°, and Jupiter conjunction Uranus at 2.1° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. These angles were checked through every hour of that civil day and survive throughout, which is why an unrecorded hour does not disturb them.

blocks.title: What the angles build
blocks.text: The day-stable angles form no closed figure. Nothing funnels; each aspect is its own negotiation, which the tradition reads as a chart of separate treaties rather than one campaign.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The classical table has four entries for this chart. The Sun in Aquarius at 22.6° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; the Moon in Taurus at 14.0° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Venus in Pisces at 4.5° is in exaltation; Saturn in Cancer at 1.8° is in detriment. None of these labels is a verdict on a person; they describe how a function is situated, nothing more.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: The certain ground: 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, dividing 5 air, 3 earth, 2 water by element and 4 fixed, 3 mutable, 3 cardinal by mode. Air signs carry exchange in the scheme — comparison, argument, the sentence that makes the situation legible. No settled placement falls in fire — an absence the tradition treats as information, not as a defect. Venus, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Pluto were retrograde — apparent backward motion from where the Earth sits, which the tradition reads as a function turned inward before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Taurus for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 13.0° between midnight and midnight. That is quick enough to make the exact degree a neighbourhood rather than an address, and slow enough to leave the sign settled. At the noon reference it stands at 14.0°.
